change: Release inlining treats a single tiny read-only leaf loop as a small function at every call site: at most 32 IR instructions, two parameters, scalar integer return, no frame slots/raw pointers/stores/opaque calls. Larger loops retain the existing caller-size cap. No surface attributes or language rules added.

validation.fuzz: 100 fresh seeds 1301..1400 across five modes (500 executions). This also closes independent bootstrap/full validation for the preceding fixed-index-domain change.

limits: All 12 laptop comparisons pass the unchanged 2% limit. Default synthetic build improves about 1.1%; compiler rebuilding costs about 1.15% more. The 250k goal remains unmet.
All 32 ordinary benchmark artifacts unchanged, with fresh independent checksums. Prior runtime evidence and unresolved timings carry forward.

Removing 768 direct prune calls shifts most of its work into callers; ordinary compiler instruction savings are 0.7–0.9%, not the full former function-attributed cost. Compiler binary grows about 0.7%.

The loop-call-sites-only prototype removed 87 prune calls with essentially flat compiler work and was superseded. Its measurements remain in the evidence. No new whole-program analysis pass or baseline promotion.
